Subject: Runtime fit & context snapshot for NimbleDocs onboarding

Hi Samira —

Thanks for the call earlier. As promised, I'm sending a concise snapshot of what we'll need to land during the implementation phase so your engineering and SRE teams can validate capacity early. High-level asks below; we can iterate if your traffic shape differs.

Quick questions for your SRE/infra folks (if you can loop them in):
- Typical document size (tokens) for the 1st-pass extraction vs. the downstream QA/edit pass?
- Percentage of calls that require long-context >8k (e.g., multi-document aggregation) vs. short-context (<=4k)?
- Expected 95th percentile RPS during campaign spikes (you mentioned marketing sends) and desired latency SLO for inference.

Initial NimbleDocs numbers you shared on the call (please confirm):
- Monthly unique users: ~150,000
- Average document tokens per request (first-pass): 320 tokens
- Fraction of requests that cascade to multi-document context: 8%
- Peak concurrent RPS (during peak campaigns): ~185 RPS sustained for ~10 minutes

What this implies (baseline estimates):
- Baseline steady-state tokens/day: 150k users * 1 req/user/day * 320 tokens = ~48M tokens/month (~1.6M tokens/day).
- Peak tokens/sec at 185 RPS * 320 tokens = ~59.2k tokens/sec (burst).
- With 8% long-context (assume 8k tokens average) additional load during those requests.

Model shortlist recommendation (first pass — engineering will validate):
1) Llama-3-13B-chat (16k) — good latency/cost balance for short->medium context and when you want deterministic output.
2) Mistral-Instruct-32k — strong quality on summarization/aggregation across longer context; higher memory but fewer tokens-per-dollar in heavy-context scenarios.
3) Quantized 8-bit variant of 70B chat (on Dedicated) — for high-quality, low-noise completions on legal/contract-heavy docs where hallucination risk must be minimized.

Operational notes:
- For the 8% long-context flows, prefer model 2 with prefix/KV caching and segmented chunking. This reduces repeated transformer work across overlapping contexts.
- Apply per-customer prompt caching for boilerplate templates (we can provide a caching config that reduces tokens-per-request by ~10-15% for templated outputs).

Attachments: I've included the traffic snapshot you shared plus a sample prompt set we tested internally.

Next steps:
- Samira: confirm/attach an SRE contact and validate the peak RPS numbers and document token sizes.
- Dev: once SRE confirms, can you start an initial inference sizing with the three model candidates above and a 2-week simulated traffic replay?
- Karthik: please add quantified rollback thresholds for the canary when we instrument latency & error budgets.

Thanks —
Maya

Thanks Alex — I pulled the CSV and ran a quick back-of-envelope sizing against our staging runtime. Notes:
- For short-context flows on Llama-3-13B-chat (16k): ~120 concurrent RPS sustained per 1 x p4d-equivalent instance to keep 95th < 300ms (with batching window = 10ms). So to cover 150 RPS sustained, plan for 2 instances for redundancy and headroom.
- For the 8% long-context requests (assume 8k tokens): these blow memory for 13B with aggressive batching. We recommend routing long-context to a separate pool running Mistral-Instruct-32k on instances sized for larger memory (1 x a40-equivalent per 40 long requests/sec).
- If NimbleDocs wants to keep everything on hosted Redwood with autoscaling, I recommend:
  * Short-context pool: 3 small instances (covers up to ~240 RPS with headroom and canary weight split).
  * Long-context pool: 1 larger instance for early testing and autoscale to 2 at 8k sustained long requests/sec spikes (rare but necessary).

Canary plan: route 5% of traffic to the new model across both pools with a rollback threshold of 1.5x error rate or 20% latency degradation at 95th. Also enable token-level cost telemetry and sample outputs to a secure bucket for quality review.

Action items:
- Maya: schedule a 2-hour workshop with your SREs and product to validate the canary thresholds and run the replay test.
- Samira/Alex: confirm a preferred 2-week window for the traffic replay.
